name: GUINEA-BISSAU

flag.title: Guinea-Bissau flag
flag.note: Red, yellow & green with a black star

lead: Guinea-Bissau is a small country in West Africa. Its coast breaks into 88 islands fringed with mangrove trees. Cashew trees cover half the land. Hippos swim in the sea, and drumbeats from 20 peoples fill the air.

sections.geography: A coast eaten by the sea

geo: Guinea-Bissau is very flat. Its highest hill is just 277 m. Twice a day, Atlantic tides flood and drain huge mudflats.
Inland, cashew orchards and rice fields stretch toward a flat, grassy highland. Nearly all of the year’s 2,000 mm of rain falls from June to October.
animals: The Bijagós Islands are a nature reserve the world protects. At night, marine hippos wade into the open Atlantic to eat sea-grass. No other hippos regularly feed in saltwater.
Over 100,000 Caspian terns (seabirds) nest on a single island, the largest waterbird colony in West Africa. Green monkeys bounce through the cashew groves.
culture: More than 20 ethnic groups live here. Gumbé, the national sound, mixes African drums with Portuguese tunes. Kora lutes and balafon xylophones join every celebration.
On the Bijagós Islands, people hold up to 100 ceremony days a year. In a coming-of-age rite called fanado, young people spend months in the forest with elders. Bijagó women own the land.
history: Portuguese traders arrived in the 1400s, and the coast became a hub of the Atlantic slave trade. Foreign rule lasted nearly 500 years.
In 1956, Amílcar Cabral founded the PAIGC liberation movement. After eleven years of fighting, independence was declared on 24 September 1973.
wows: Guinea-Bissau declared independence in 1973, a year before Portugal accepted it.
The Bijagó people see the marine hippos as sacred ancestors.
Its name adds the capital, Bissau, to tell it apart from Guinea.
Cashew nuts make up most of what Guinea-Bissau sells abroad.
Guinea-Bissau has had over nine coups (forced takeovers) or tries since 1974, among the most anywhere.
It is one of the world's least-visited countries.
Bijagó women traditionally choose their own husbands.

myths.myth: Cashew nuts grow inside the cashew fruit
myths.fact: The nut hangs below a juicy fruit called the cashew apple. The raw shell has an oil that burns skin, so workers roast it first.

myths.myth: Trees cannot grow in salty water
myths.fact: Mangroves can. Their roots block most salt, and their leaves push out the rest. The tangled roots also shelter baby fish.
